reading.body:
Alexandria Paolozzi Moore appears on six AI lobbying filings, all filed through one firm, all for a single client, FDD ACTION.

The pattern is narrow rather than broad. Six filings, one firm, one client. The sixteen bills named across those filings are the substance of the record, and they span both chambers and both HR and S numbering. A lobbyist working one client through one firm is a concentrated assignment, not a portfolio.

For AI specifically, this is one of the channels through which compute and power policy gets written. Data center siting, grid interconnection, and federal permitting all move through bills like these, and the filings are the public trace of who is in the room when they move. The disclosed prior government position, an internship in a House office in 2010, is the only biographical fact the record carries.

What the data does not tell the reader is what was said, what was sought, or what any bill would do. It records that a name appears on filings, not influence, outcomes, or positions. It also covers only AI-tagged filings held by this site, so any lobbying on other subjects is outside the count.
